title: Implement kinetic model and fitting
action: Write a Python script to implement the kinetic mechanism (Scheme 1A) as a system of ODEs using the provided rate constants (except the adjustable ones) and experimental conditions (temperatures, pressures, initial concentrations). Use a numerical ODE solver (e.g., solve_ivp from SciPy) to simulate species concentrations over time. Fit the unknown rate constants k2, k8, and kui by minimizing the sum of squared differences between simulated and the provided experimental yields and conversions at 723 K. Employ an optimization routine (e.g., scipy.optimize.minimize).
description: This step implements the kinetic simulation and optimizes the three key rate constants to match the experimental data at 723 K. The optimized values serve as input for the subsequent RRKM calculations.

title: RRKM falloff calculations
action: Using the fitted low-pressure rate constants k2 and k8 from step_01, the high-pressure A-factor estimates, vibrational frequencies and collision parameters from the paper's appendix, perform RRKM calculations to extract the high-pressure activation energies E2 and E8 and the temperature-dependent rate constants k2(T) and k8(T) at 695, 723, and 748 K.
description: This step performs the RRKM analysis to determine the high-pressure activation energies and falloff curves for the ethylsilylene decomposition and isomerization.

title: Compute thermochemical quantities
action: From the high-pressure activation energy E2, the known heats of formation of reactants and products, and the fitted rate constants, calculate the heat of formation of ethylsilylene (ΔHf°(EtSiH)) and the methylene group additivity value (C-(H)2(C,Si)). Output all final derived quantities as a single JSON file.
description: Final scored output containing the fitted rate constants, high-pressure activation energies, and thermochemical parameters. This step is load-bearing.
